To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of the proposed pilot RCT is feasible and will be able to determine the feasibility of a future definitive RACT on the effectiveness of an online toolbox for employers to support the RTW of cancer survivors.
the proposed design for a pilot RCT to study whether the MiLES intervention is feasible to study the successful RTW in cancer survivors is feasible and that a future definitive RRC is warranted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for improving the RTW of people with cancer, namely by targeting employers.
the development of a new intervention for employers to support the return to work of their employees with cancer.
the development and evaluation of an online toolbox targeting the employer to support the RTW process for employees diagnosed with cancer (MiLES).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MiLES intervention is feasible for a future definitive randomised controlled trial to study the effectiveness on the successful return to work for cancer survivors in paid employment.
the MiLES intervention is a feasible intervention that can be used to support employers in the return to work of their employees with cancer.
this pilot RCT can potentially increase the probability of successful future RCTs and can obviate the necessity of an unfeasible, resource-intensive and potentially unsuccessful study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a new intervention, we have a new study design and we have a new way of thinking.
we will determine the feasibility to conduct a future RCT on the effects of the MiLES online toolbox on successful RTW.
the MiLES intervention was developed to target employers during the RT to work process of cancer survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to carry out an RCT to study whether an online toolbox for employers supporting employees diagnosed with cancer to successfully return to work is effective.

the design of a feasibility study can be used to determine whether a definitive RCT is needed to study the effectiveness and efficiency of an intervention on successful RT to work of employees diagnosed with a chronic disease such as cancer.
it is important for researchers to be aware of the importance of the feasibility study in the research process.
